scope: Read only b233 candidate/investigation and checked-in platform statement. Only peer-review-b233.json is written; no source/candidate/investigation edits.

proofReview.reason: Deleting intervals cannot improve a full assignment. Conversely, every subset using each device at most once extends by arbitrary orientations of unused devices without decreasing coverage. These two inequalities establish equal optimal values.

proofReview.claim: Strict endpoint order in an irredundant family
proofReview.reason: After deletion to inclusion-minimal coverage, no interval is contained in another. Equal left or equal right endpoints would give containment, including exact duplicates; therefore sorting by right endpoints makes both endpoints strictly increasing. Zero-length arms are safely omitted.

With l_H<l_I<l_J and r_H<r_I<r_J, if r_H>=l_J, H and J overlap or touch and their union covers I completely. Thus I is deletable. Closed endpoints do not rescue equality: they have zero length and the touching union already contains the meeting point.

proofReview.verdict: correct ONLY together with strict triple condition
proofReview.reason: A device has L ending at x and R beginning at x. If adjacent, the explicit device check rejects them. If one or more intervals intervene, the penultimate interval h before R has r_h>=x by strictly increasing right endpoints, whereas adding R requires r_h<l_R=x. Contradiction. This also explains why a maximum-valued prefix never hides a conflicting earlier device.

proofReview.claim: Gain depends only on last interval
proofReview.reason: For l_i<l_j and r_i<r_j, every older interval ends no later than r_i. If r_i<=l_j, J contributes its whole length. Otherwise I itself covers J from l_j to r_i, so the new contribution is exactly r_j-r_i. This is r_j-max(l_j,r_i).

For last pair (i,j), the previous interval h must have h<i and r_h<l_j. q=bisect_left(allRights,l_j) counts exactly r_h<l_j. P[i][min(q,i)] includes precisely h<min(q,i), and also the one-interval base len_i. Conditions l_i<l_j, r_i<r_j and distinct adjacent devices are separately checked.

proofReview.claim: Initialization / inclusive prefix index / final answer
proofReview.reason: Row j has j+1 cells. row[0]=len_j represents no predecessor. After processing predecessor i, row[i+1] is the maximum over predecessors 0..i and the singleton. Thus P[j][t] has predecessor index <t, including P[0][0]. Taking max over all final rows plus singleton values finds all nonempty chains; all-zero input returns 0 before table construction.

Every original optimum has an equal-union irredundant chain, which DP enumerates. Every DP chain has unique device IDs by the preceding lemma and therefore extends to a valid full orientation assignment, giving the opposite inequality.

The proof does not require distinct anchors or sorted input. Ties in either endpoint cannot appear together in a minimal chain. Different devices with equal arms are still distinguished when taking opposite orientations. Zero arms have no positive measure and may be dropped.

All arms lie in [-10^9,2*10^9]; coverage and valid DP values are <=3*10^9, so uint32_t is sufficient but signed int32 is not. C++ gains and coordinates use long long. M<=10000 gives 50005000 uint32 cells, exactly 200020000 bytes; O(N) containers/input overhead is additional.

independentValidation.oracle: Compressed endpoint atoms with integer weights; propagate the two orientation choices per device and deduplicate complete union masks. No irredundant-chain or DP assumptions are used.

weakeningCounterexamples.claim: Changing strict triple to r_H<=l_J, or omitting the triple test while forbidding only adjacent equal IDs
weakeningCounterexamples.reason: The four arms alternate device IDs and have strict endpoint order, but repeat both devices. Each triple has equality r_H=l_J, so the original strict condition correctly rejects it.

performanceReview.assessment: The proof establishes O(N^2), not 5-second Python acceptance. The supplied snapshot reports 14-24 seconds at N=5000; retain this caveat until national2 optimization is independently rebenchmarked. This review does not modify or optimize the candidate.
performanceReview.optimizedPythonSecondPhase: See optimizedPythonSecondPhase: four independent N5000 runs (including nested frontier) and explicit retained quadratic bound; earlier pre-optimization timings do not describe this code.

proofCritique: The proof is sound; explicitly retain strict < in the triple and both endpoint comparisons. The equality counterexample is worth keeping as a regression test.
Explain the penultimate-interval argument when claiming adjacent device IDs suffice: that implication is false without the triple invariant.
Keep the table contract predecessor index <t visible next to min(q,i); replacing lower_bound with upper_bound is not a harmless optimization.
Do not narrow table entries or answer to signed int32; the source permits a 3000000000 answer.

proofReview.critique: At a fixed anchor only the longest selected left and right arms affect union. Their lengths can be dominated by the two largest real distinct devices, assigning the longer device to the longer required side. Tied lengths must still represent two distinct devices; code increments IDs for each retained positive length, so it does.

The online minimum update maintains the smallest left endpoint for each of the two best distinct device IDs. Decreasing either stored minimum and swapping second into first is sufficient; an untracked device cannot improve an excluded-device query unless it enters the best two. Exhaustively compared exclusion minima on captured prefixes.

q_j=0 means no endpoint is strictly below l_j; hence a predecessor has r_i>=l_j and its prior P[i][0]=len_i. Valid gain simplifies to r_j-l_i. Prefixes must be capped before the first equal-right interval and exclude device_j, exactly as starts/min1/min2/owner1 do. If the excluded minimum is >=l_j no valid predecessor exists; kind0 is constant for all prefixes.

For i<q_j intervals end strictly before l_j; an ending chain at i can safely append j with its full length. It cannot contain j's other arm, whose right endpoint is >=l_j. Thus the global prefix maximum is valid. For 0<t<=q_j use len_j+global_best[t-1]; t=0 remains len_j.

Every later requested positive q<row_index belongs to global queries and is >= suffix_min[row_index+1], so its rank lies at or after offset and below the computed hi. q>=row_index uses end_best. Entries <=current q are filled by the disjoint formula; scanning predecessor i stores prefix i+1. The rank coordinate is global and stable across rows.

Any chain ending at j is contained in [minLeftPrefix[j+1],right_j], so the hull width upper bounds every prefix value. Upon equality all later prefixes have the same maximum. After stop only equal-right predecessors remain and are forbidden, also making a constant tail. tail=write is the first unstored global rank; already written entries retain their actual earlier-prefix values.

There are O(M) rows, each scanning at most M predecessors and writing at most M selected prefix values, with O(1) compressed lookups and O(log M) setup bisections. Preprocessing sorting/bisection O(M log M); total O(N^2) time and worst-case O(N^2) memory, including array capacity plus O(N) objects/input token storage. These optimizations give no subquadratic or universal deadline guarantee; Python hash-map grouping assumes usual constant-time integer dict operations. No DP hash lookups are used.

independentValidation.oracle: Weighted coordinate-compressed elementary-segment masks propagated for exactly one arm per original device; no same-anchor reduction and no interval-chain recurrence in oracle.

maxNRuntimeCases.name: same_anchor_top_two
maxNRuntimeCases.reason: Two longest arms on opposite sides attain the sum; no orientation can exceed it.

maxNRuntimeCases.name: separated_arms
maxNRuntimeCases.reason: All device envelopes disjoint: sum of lengths is invariant.

maxNRuntimeCases.name: equal_length_unique_anchors
maxNRuntimeCases.reason: Global hull [-10^9,10^9+4999] attained by left arms at0,4998 and right arms at1,4999.

maxNRuntimeCases.name: nested_unique_anchor_frontier
maxNRuntimeCases.reason: If the last device points right, every available left endpoint is at least -L-(N-2), yielding upper bound 2L+4N-5. If it points left, every available right endpoint is at most L+3(N-2), giving the smaller bound 2L+4N-7. Left arm at N-2 and right arms at N-3 and N-1 cover the larger hull continuously, attaining the first bound.

proofCritique: Preserve strict r_h<l_j and strict r_i<r_j from the first-phase proof; none of these optimizations permits endpoint equality.
Keep two distinct devices at coincident anchors, even when lengths tie. Keeping only the longest arm loses valid two-sided coverage.
Sparse table indices are global query ranks, not local predecessor indices; offset, first unstored tail rank and suffix lower bound must change together.

Quadratic worst-case bounds remain honest. Max-N checks are measured examples, not a proof of passing all deployed-machine deadlines. Array allocation overhead and input tokens remain additional memory.

Correctness approved, worst-case complexity remains quadratic.
